stem:
A capacitor of capacitance 470 μF is connected to a battery of electromotive force (e.m.f.) 24 V in the circuit of Fig. 5.1.

[[fig:f1]]

The two-way switch S is initially at position X.

P and Q are identical long straight wires, each with a resistance of 5.6 kΩ. These wires are placed near to, and parallel to, each other. Wire Q is connected to a voltmeter.

At time *t* = 0, switch S is moved to position Y so that the capacitor discharges through wire P.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: Calculate the charge *Q*₀ on the capacitor at time *t* = 0.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Calculate the current *I*₀ in wire P at time *t* = 0.

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text: Calculate the time constant *τ* of the discharge circuit.

parts.label: (a)(iv)
parts.text:
On Fig. 5.2, sketch a line to show the variation with *t* of the current *I* in wire P as the capacitor discharges.

[[fig:f2]]

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Explain why there is an induced e.m.f. across wire Q during the discharge of the capacitor.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
On Fig. 5.3, sketch a line to suggest the variation with *t* of the voltmeter reading *V*.

[[fig:f3]]

figures.caption: Fig. 5.1
figures.alt: A circuit diagram shows a capacitor and battery connected through a two-way switch, with wire P and wire Q drawn parallel and a voltmeter connected across Q.

figures.caption: Fig. 5.2
figures.alt: Blank current-versus-time axes, with current I on the vertical axis, time t on the horizontal axis, and I₀ marked on the vertical axis.

figures.caption: Fig. 5.3
figures.alt: Blank voltmeter-reading-versus-time axes, with V on the vertical axis and t on the horizontal axis.
